problems.statement: The 98.1% on-time figure is largely an artifact of the bonus-driven rewriting of promised dates (KPI uses the revised date), not a real improvement in delivery performance.

The incentive plan tied to a gameable KPI definition, with no change to revision permissions or controls, created the incentive and means to reset dates; revisions jumped 5x exactly when the bonus took effect at each center (Mar 2026 Northgate/Riverside, Jul 2026 Pell Junction).
RouteWise caused the on-time improvement (CEO's explanation).
Revisions are legitimate responses to customer requests and weather (dispatch manager's explanation).

Actual service to customers has not improved and has probably worsened (lateness complaints up, Brightwell on-time against original booking fell 87% to 81%), with a customer-loss risk (30% of the largest customer's lanes going to tender) and a misleading-advertising risk.
The rise in lateness complaints is merely a portal reporting artifact.

A driver shortage (capacity) is a genuine contributor to real lateness and some legitimate capacity-related revisions, particularly on mountain lanes, but is not established as the main driver of the revision spike.

Late revisions with little customer notification mean customers are not told about changes, so the dispatch-side date reset shifts the cost of lateness onto customers and hides it from management and the KPI.
Supervisory culture and the absence of a speak-up channel sustain the gaming; concerns are rarely raised.

causalClaims.from: Dispatcher on-time bonus tied to revisable promised-date KPI
causalClaims.to: Surge in promised-date revisions (esp. Operational-Capacity, late-entered, non-notified)
Lower miles and fuel cost per shipment

causalClaims.from: Gamed on-time metric and unannounced date changes

actions.action: Do not launch the '98 out of 100, on time' campaign on the current metric; substantiating it would be misleading.
actions.rationale: The figure counts against revised dates and the customer's own receiving data shows about 81% on time against the original booking.

actions.action: Do not raise the bonus tier to $1,500 at 99% on the existing KPI definition.
actions.rationale: It would increase the incentive to rewrite dates while the metric stays gameable.

actions.action: Recompute on-time against the original promised date (and customer-requested date) from the revision log, by center, lane and quarter, as the primary KPI.
actions.rationale: This gives the true performance baseline and is cheap to do from existing data.

actions.action: Freeze or suspend the on-time bonus, or re-base it on the original-date measure, and add controls on revisions (approval, mandatory customer notification, audit of Operational-Capacity resets).
actions.rationale: This removes the incentive and the means of gaming that created the distortion.

actions.action: Contact Brightwell and other major accounts proactively with accurate on-time data and a recovery plan before the Q1 tender review.
actions.rationale: Revenue at risk is large and the customer already sees the gap.

actions.action: Address driver shortage on mountain lanes through recruitment and retention and capacity planning.
actions.rationale: Likely a real contributor to lateness but its size is not yet quantified.

actions.action: Review the bonus payouts already made and the integrity of the Q3 scorecards sent to customers (including the 98.4% sent to Brightwell).
actions.rationale: Addresses disclosure and legal exposure, but follows the metric rebuild.

actions.action: Attribute the improvement to RouteWise and expand it for on-time reasons.
actions.rationale: RouteWise shows fuel and mileage benefit only, and on-time rose at centers before RouteWise at Northgate.
The behavior responds to a system incentive and supervisor direction, and punishing individuals would not fix the design.

nextEvidence: On-time performance against original promised date for all shipments by center, lane and month, Jan 2025 to Oct 2026, from the revision log
Notification and complaint records and shipment-level data from other large accounts to test whether Brightwell's experience generalizes
Driver-vacancy-adjusted analysis of revisions and original-date lateness by lane, to size the real capacity contribution
output.summary: The 98.1% on-time figure is mainly a measurement artifact. The bonus plan paid on a KPI measured against a revisable promised date, with no revision controls. Revisions rose fivefold at each center exactly when the bonus took effect, shifting to capacity-coded, late-entered, mostly unnotified changes. RouteWise went live at Northgate only in October and shows fuel and mileage benefits, not on-time. The largest customer measures 81% on time against original bookings, down from 87%, and lateness complaints are up. Do not launch the campaign or raise the bonus. Rebuild the KPI on original dates, add revision controls, and protect key accounts. Driver shortage is a real but unsized contributor.
